description: Registry of empirical reference levels for paper-rubric-review. Each level is a JSON file containing the score distribution of n papers that achieved a defined external milestone (e.g., accepted to a specific journal volume). Levels are NOT tier predictions — they are observational reference data so a scored paper can be compared to the empirical distribution of papers known to have hit that milestone.

levels.level_name_en: YSA Yuanpei Young Scholars Journal Vol.10 (April 2026) — STEM
levels.level_name_zh: YSA 元培青年学者期刊 第 10 期 (2026 年 4 月) — STEM 方向

steps: 1. Score n>=5 papers that share a specific external milestone (e.g., accepted to Vol.X of journal Y) using the paper-rubric-review protocol.
2. Compute per-dim statistics (min, q1, median, mean, q3, max, std) and macro stats (research, paper, potential) and total.
3. Save as JSON following the schema in ysa10-stem.json (or use the script in scripts/build-calibration.py).
4. Add a new entry to this registry with: level_id, level_name, n_papers, milestone_type, summary.
5. Document provenance: who scored, when, protocol version, noise estimate.
how_to_add_new_level.minimum_n_recommendation: n>=5 for any usable IQR. n>=10 for stable medians. n>=20 for cross-year stability.
honest_framing_rules: NEVER use 'tier X is the threshold' language. Always say 'level X contains papers that achieved milestone M'.
NEVER extrapolate beyond observed data (no 'X score means Yau gold' — no Yau calibration exists).
Always include the noise estimate (±8 points) when showing comparisons.
Always disclose the selection process (e.g., 'all 12 STEM papers in Vol.10' — not 'top STEM papers').
